data.title: Bulk Let's Encrypt Certificate Issuance Clustering
data.description: Detects clusters of Let's Encrypt certificate issuances for domains sharing nameserver or registrar characteristics within a short time window. RDGA and AI-generated campaigns frequently provision certificates in bulk immediately after registration to enable HTTPS on fraudulent landing pages and phishing sites. Legitimate bulk certificate issuance typically occurs through established organizations with consistent registration history. This rule identifies anomalous spikes in certificate issuance where multiple domains share infrastructure indicators such as common nameservers, registrar, or IP allocation, and certificates are issued within hours of domain registration. The combination of rapid registration-to-certificate timing and shared infrastructure strongly indicates coordinated fraudulent domain provisioning for campaign deployment.

enrichment_required.source: Certificate analytics enrichment (time between registration and cert issuance)

falsepositives: Large-scale legitimate deployments using automated certificate provisioning (e.g., SaaS platforms onboarding customer domains)
Hosting providers that auto-provision Let's Encrypt certificates for new customer sites
CDN providers issuing certificates for newly onboarded domains
